questions.question: Which sequence best represents the critical path for this design?
options: Analytics dashboard -> global lock -> one shared database -> user response.
Post event -> hybrid fan-out and candidate stores -> ranking -> timeline cache -> reader response.
User request -> synchronous batch retraining -> manual review -> response.
Client -> every regional service -> global consensus -> unbounded retry loop.
questions.explanation: The lesson's critical path is Post event -> hybrid fan-out and candidate stores -> ranking -> timeline cache -> reader response.

questions.question: Which statement captures the central correctness or safety invariant?
options: Every subsystem must provide strong global consistency for every field.
Availability always takes priority, even when a request violates policy or ownership rules.
Visibility and block rules are enforced at read time even when precomputed timelines contain stale candidates.
A high average success rate makes per-request correctness unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Visibility and block rules are enforced at read time even when precomputed timelines contain stale candidates.

questions.question: What is the most defensible degraded-mode strategy?
options: Retry every failed dependency without a limit until it recovers.
Skip correctness and safety checks so the request can still complete.
Send all fallback traffic to one primary dependency with no admission control.
Fall back from ranking to a recent safe timeline and contain celebrity fan-out with pull-based delivery.
questions.explanation: Fall back from ranking to a recent safe timeline and contain celebrity fan-out with pull-based delivery.

questions.question: Why should the critical path and invariant be designed before choosing vendors?
options: They expose what must be fast, what must never be violated, and where bounded degradation is acceptable.
They guarantee one vendor will satisfy every workload without measurement.
They remove the need for capacity estimates, failure tests, and observability.
They make storage, consistency, and retry semantics interchangeable.
questions.explanation: Architecture choices are defensible only when they follow explicit user-visible goals, invariants, and failure boundaries.
